caption: Uber Eats and Postmates compared asset by asset at announcement: 400K partnered restaurants and 111M MAPCs against 115K merchants, 10M+ customers and a subscription running 30%+ of Postmates orders.
Uber Freight's pre-deal economics: revenue $67M in 2017 to a $1,205M Q1 2021 run rate, a 106% CAGR, with EBITDA margin improving from (60)% to (10)%.
Where managed transportation sits above brokerage in the freight value chain, and the layer Uber Freight bought into with Transplace.
Marketplace liquidity made visible: US active drivers +67% since January 2021 cut surged trips from 25% to 6% and wait times from 7.4 to 4.7 minutes.
Mobility take rate and segment margin by quarter from Q3 2019 with the UK driver-classification accrual stripped out; margin returned to 2019 levels on 21% lower Gross Bookings.
The 2019-2021 portfolio reshaping: India Eats to Zomato, JUMP to Lime, ATG to Aurora, Elevate to Joby, 15+ sub-scale delivery markets exited, against $1B of run-rate fixed-cost reduction.
Price per US trip across the ladder: Uber Black $48, UberX $16, UberX Share $12, public transport about $2 at 7x Uber's trip volume, personal vehicles about $0.50 per mile at 6.6B weekly trips.
Management's autonomy thesis in one chart: rideshare is under 1% of US urban vehicle miles, and a $1.00 per mile AV price would open roughly 25x that addressable base.
Delivery at Q4 2021: $54B run-rate Gross Bookings, leading positions in 7 of the top 10 markets, and 80% of global Gross Bookings in markets that gained category position.
Uber Freight positioned as the largest digital freight marketplace: $17B of freight under management with Transplace, claimed #1 on operational efficiency and digital fleet.
The cross-app acquisition advantage quantified: the Uber Rides app brought in 2.1x the Delivery consumers of all paid channels combined, at 25% of paid-channel cost.
Quarterly platform Gross Bookings per consumer in Q4 2021: $58 Mobility, $151 Delivery, $364 cross-platform.
The origin of the advertising business: $11M of revenue in 2020, $141M in 2021, and a $1B+ target for 2024 with the ad surfaces and formats named.
The long-term segment margin targets management has been measured against since: Mobility 25% take rate x 45% EBITDA margin = 11.25% of Gross Bookings, Delivery 15% x 30% = 4.5%.
Unit economics of markets already at target margin: driver payments take 73% of Mobility Gross Bookings and driver plus merchant payments 82% of Delivery's, leaving 15% and 8% contribution.
The three-year frame set in 2022: FY2018 $58B Gross Bookings at (3.7)% Adjusted EBITDA margin, FY2021 $90B at (0.9)%, FY2024 target $165-175B and about $5B.
Uber Moto as the low-cost entry product: live in 20 countries, trips up over 100% YoY, active Moto drivers up over 60%, and 40% of Moto riders go on to another Mobility product.
Cross-promotion between the two apps: 31% of Delivery first trips originate in the Mobility app and 22% the reverse, at half the cost of paid channels.
Monthly consumer penetration by country against population 18+; matching UK penetration would add about $13B of US Gross Bookings and Mexico's would add about $11B in India.
How management frames Uber's value to AV developers, with the hybrid human-plus-AV network and go-to-market as the argument, and 10 live AV partnerships as of February 2024.
Market-level profitability: 85% of top-ten countries profitable in both segments, Mobility top ten at 7% of Gross Bookings and Delivery top ten at 2%, with most still below best-in-class.
What separates free cash flow from Adjusted EBITDA, including the captive insurer whose reserve growth is restricted cash driven by US Mobility trip growth and insurance cost.
The capital allocation framework as first published, with a ~2x gross leverage target and investment grade ratings, alongside the inaugural $7B repurchase authorization.
Grocery and Retail restates Delivery's addressable market: about $2T of food against about $10T of grocery and retail in markets Uber Eats already operates.
Grocery and Retail's platform effect: 7% of Delivery's first-time users, monthly platform frequency from 4.8 to 6.1 for adopters, and about $12B of Gross Bookings run-rate.
Mobility trip growth in Atlanta and Austin accelerated after AV launch relative to the US top 20 cities, with first-time riders +9pp and trips per rider +3pp.

The demand-variability argument against an AV-only competitor: a typical Monday is about 45% of a Saturday and daily troughs about 5% of peaks, with AVs as fixed base load and human drivers as boost supply.
Uber operates in 8,000+ US markets covering 95% of the population, and the top 20 cities account for only about 30% of US Mobility Gross Bookings and about 25% of US Mobility profits.
The Mobility barbell: low-cost products deliver 75% higher frequency, premium products 3.5x the profit dollars of standard-only users, and together over 25% of first-time Mobility users.
Delivery Hero terms: EUR 41.50 per share, $14.8bn equity value, about 8x EV/2027E Adjusted EBITDA including synergies, 50% plus one share minimum acceptance, H2 2027 close.
Pro forma scale on management's own peer set: $236B of 2025 Gross Bookings and $9.8B of Adjusted EBITDA, against Eternal, Lyft, Grab, Prosus, Instacart, Didi and DoorDash combined.

How the deal is financed and pared back: about EUR 14bn committed bridge, gross leverage kept below 2x, and 14 Delivery Hero markets with about $11bn of Gross Bookings sold to SSW Partners with Uber lending most of the price.

Uber One's engagement economics in mid-2026: 400K participating merchants up about 50% YoY, merchant-funded offers up about 70%, and about 40% of eligible members active across both Mobility and Delivery.
